episodes.167571: A strong upper-level low impacted Southern California on March 28th and 29th. Widespread precipitation occurred with this system, with areas of heavy rain at lower elevations and snow in the mountains. Heavy rain in spots led to flooding, which then led to some water rescues, road closures, as well as a small mud and debris flow on the Bond Fire burn scar.
episodes.167803: An unstable air mass developed as an upper trough moved into the area.

events.narrative: Heavy rain began on the morning of March 28th and continued through the afternoon on March 29th. Rainfall of 0.50 to 1.00 inches fell across much of coastal and inland valley locations in Orange County, with far southeastern portions of Orange County as well as the foothills and mountains receiving upwards of 1.50 to 2.00 inches.

Heavy rain began on the morning of March 28th and continued through the afternoon on March 29th. Rainfall of 0.75 to 1.50 inches fell across much of coastal and valley locations in San Diego County, with far southern portions of San Diego County as well as the foothills and mountains receiving 1.50 to 2.00 inches.

Heavy rain began on the morning of March 28th and lasted through the afternoon on March 29th. Widespread rainfall totals of around 0.50 inch to nearly 1.00 inch were observed across Riverside County, with localized areas in the mountains seeing rainfall totals near 1.50 inches.

Heavy rain began on the morning of March 28th and lasted through the afternoon on March 29th. Widespread rainfall totals of around 0.50 inch to nearly 1.00 inch were observed across the lower elevations in San Bernardino County, with localized areas in the mountains seeing rainfall totals anywhere from 1.50 to 3.00 inches.
